mission: SUPERVISOR WAVE C — Z2 RED ADVERSARIAL NF525 cross-cut (hostile read-only)
evidence_mode: static-source + live read-only mysql + prior-cycle artefact dispute
verdict_rationale: N2 alone (no signed NF525-conformant Z PDF blade exists; the only PDF on disk is self-labeled 'Document interne — Synthèse NON-fiscale') is a NF525 art. 286-I-3 bis CGI conformity gap, not 'P2 polish' as the prior Z2 agent's z-close-pdf.json CAV-2 downgraded it. URSSAF / DGFiP day-1 audit would refuse the EOD PDF as the fiscal artefact AND find no fiscal artefact in any printable form. Additional N1/N5/N6/N7 surface latent risks documented as P1/P2 hardening below.

prior_z2_agents_dispute.refund.json: S1+S3 PASS confirmed empirically. NOT DISPUTED on what was tested. Disputed for SCOPE GAP: S2 partial-refund 'NOT_SUPPORTED_BY_SERVICE' is buried as informational; for NF525 it is acceptable (all-or-nothing mirror is conservative), but for V1 LOCAL UX it is a known cashier-blocker on real refund (drop 1 frite from 3-item order = must refund whole order = bigger NF525 negative + bigger customer perception of error). Flag as V1.0.2 backlog, not a NF525 violation.
prior_z2_agents_dispute.z-close-pdf.json: PASS verdict DISPUTED. CAV-1 ('two PDF endpoints, two contracts') and CAV-2 ('SIRET absent V1 LOCAL config gap') are downgraded as informational/P2. RED: both together = the system has NO signed NF525-compliant fiscal Z PDF at all. The blade itself disclaims 'non-fiscale' (line 186). NEEDS_HARDENING is the honest verdict.

findings.title: MySQL BEFORE DELETE trigger does NOT block TRUNCATE on audit_logs / z_reports
file_line: database/migrations/2026_04_22_000002_create_audit_logs_table.php:97-115 (BEFORE UPDATE/DELETE only)
database/migrations/2026_05_09_160000_add_z_reports_delete_trigger_immutability.php:30-31 (acknowledges TRUNCATE bypasses triggers)
CLAUDE.md §8 references Ansible task CVP0-1 commit f840c3ef5 as GRANT-level REVOKE mitigation
findings.reproduction: mysql -uroot foodking -e 'TRUNCATE TABLE audit_logs' (sandbox-denied in this cycle; behaviour is well-known MySQL semantics — TRUNCATE = metadata DDL, fires no row triggers). Detection IS preserved by FiscalChainValidator on next Z.open() because chain becomes empty (genesis prev_hash mismatch on next Z) — but evidence is permanently destroyed AND fiscal:verify-chain returns 'CHAIN OK' on the empty chain (no rows = no errors). Operator opens a Z and sees normal behaviour.
findings.what_prior_agents_said: Not surfaced. CLAUDE.md §8 documents the GRANT REVOKE mitigation but no in-app boot guard or runtime probe verifies the GRANT state at production startup.
findings.what_red_disputes: Mitigation lives OUTSIDE the codebase (Ansible). No AppServiceProvider boot guard checks SHOW GRANTS FOR @CURRENT_USER for absence of DROP/TRUNCATE on audit_logs|z_reports. If operator forgets the Ansible task, or future migration recreates the user with default grants, the immutability claim silently collapses. Add boot-guard probe (RuntimeException refusing prod boot if CURRENT_USER has DROP or TRUNCATE on the two tables). Today: blocked-by-policy, not blocked-by-code.
findings.remediation: AppServiceProvider production boot-guard: SELECT PRIVILEGE_TYPE FROM information_schema.USER_PRIVILEGES + table-grants; throw if DROP|REFERENCES|TRUNCATE present on audit_logs|z_reports. Mirrors the existing POS_SIMULATION_HARDWARE / CACHE_DRIVER pattern.

resources/views/pdf/eod_synthesis.blade.php:186 verbatim disclaimer: 'Document interne — Synthèse non-fiscale. Pour la clôture fiscale officielle, se référer au Rapport Z journalier signé HMAC (NF525, art. 286-I-3 bis du CGI). Conservation 6 ans.'

findings.what_prior_agents_said: z-close-pdf.json CAV-1: 'two PDF endpoints, two contracts ... informational'. CAV-2: 'SIRET absent V1 LOCAL config gap, P2 polish'. Verdict was Z_LIVE_VERIFIED PASS.
findings.what_red_disputes: The 'two PDF endpoints' framing hides the truth: there is ONE PDF endpoint (EOD synthese) and ONE JSON endpoint (signed bundle). NEITHER renders a fiscal-compliant printable Z. NF525 art. 286-I-3 bis CGI requires the daily Z to be reproducible from the signed payload — i.e. the operator/auditor must be able to print/verify the Z. The signed JSON bundle IS the fiscal artefact in theory but has no human-printable form. The EOD PDF self-disclaims 'non-fiscale'. This is a code-level missing-feature, not a config polish.
findings.remediation: Create resources/views/pdf/z_report.blade.php with the 8 NF525 fields above. Wire from ZReportController::pdf() with a ?format=pdf query parameter (keep JSON for API consumers, PDF for printable). Add SIRET to config/company.php + .env scaffold + Settings UI. Render TVA breakdown from z_reports.total_by_tax_rate JSON column. Print signature_prefix + prev_hash_prefix in footer.

file_line: routes/api.php:961 Route::post('/{order}/refund-with-counter-entry') uses RMB → automatic 404 on missing model
app/Services/Order/RefundWithCounterEntryService.php:86-91 status==RETURNED guard (belt)
app/Http/Controllers/Admin/PosOrderController.php:102-108 catches QueryException 23000 → 409 MIRROR_ALREADY_EXISTS (suspenders, from migration 2026_05_19_200000 UNIQUE(orders.parent_order_id))

findings.title: Two simultaneous close attempts: defense-in-depth (Cache::lock + ZReport::lockForUpdate + status='open' WHERE on first row)
file_line: ZReportService.php:191-197 Cache::lock('z_report_b{N}') TTL 10s, ACQUIRE 4s
ZReportService.php:205-208 ZReport::query->where(status=OPEN)->lockForUpdate()->first() inside DB transaction
ZReportService.php:210-212 throws RuntimeException 'no open Z report to close for branch X' if second arrives after first commits
findings.what_red_disputes: Race protection is correct (lock + tx + lockForUpdate triple-defense). CAVEAT: under cache outage (CLAUDE.md §8 production guards forbid array/null drivers, but file driver passes — cross-process file-cache semantics on local FS are OS-dependent), Cache::lock can degenerate. The DB lockForUpdate + status='open' WHERE is the ultimate floor — losing party gets 'no open Z report to close' which is a noisy but safe failure mode. P2 hardening: add a fiscal:health-probe command verifying Cache::lock cross-process semantics on chosen driver before production boot.

findings.title: Refund of order inside current OPEN Z window → SealedOrderGuard::assertSealed throws 422 → cashier MUST use standard pre-Z path (changeStatus → RETURNED)
file_line: app/Services/Order/SealedOrderGuard.php:84-114 assertSealed throws InvalidArgumentException 422
app/Services/Order/RefundWithCounterEntryService.php:73-74 calls assertSealed('refund-with-counter-entry')
ZReportService.php:355-357 aggregate() excludes status IN (CANCELED, REJECTED, RETURNED) so pre-Z RETURNED orders correctly drop out of Z totals
findings.reproduction: Prior S3 PASS evidence proves the 422 rejection. Refund must take pre-Z path. Z aggregate then correctly excludes the RETURNED order via terminal_status whitelist (NOT via separate negative). Z totals adjust by NOT counting the order — different mathematical path than post-Z mirror counter-entry.
findings.what_red_disputes: Logic is correct. OBSERVABILITY GAP: the 422 is surfaced to the cashier as a message, but no audit_logs row is written when a pre-Z RETURNED transition happens via OrderService::changeStatus. The post-Z mirror writes 'order.refund.counter_entry' (service:301-316); the pre-Z RETURNED path does NOT have a symmetric 'order.refund.pre_z' audit row. URSSAF would expect a refund event on BOTH paths. Verify OrderService::changeStatus audit-trail coverage and add equivalent audit_logs write for pre-Z RETURNED transitions.

findings.title: Post-Z new order receives next fiscal_sequence_no with no gap, no overlap (algorithmically guaranteed)
file_line: app/Services/Fiscal/FiscalSequenceService.php:97-103 MAX(fiscal_sequence_no) +1 per branch, WHERE branch_id=X WITHOUT BranchScope + withTrashed()
Cache::lock + lockForUpdate + DB UNIQUE(orders_branch_fiscal_seq_unique) triple-defense
findings.what_red_disputes: Algorithm is correct. Two latent risks: (a) FiscalSequenceService:97 uses withTrashed (per LOCK_FISCAL_WGS_Z6_P1 2026-05-19 documented exception) so soft-deleted post-allocation orders ARE considered — good. (b) ZReportService::aggregate at line 337 uses BranchScope bypass + withTrashed too — symmetric, good. CAVEAT: no empirical proof in this cycle that creating a new order AFTER a Z close gets next seq (CAV-4 of prior z-close-pdf agent acknowledged this DEFERRED_TO_SENTINEL). FiscalSequenceMonotonicityTest sentinel covers static; physical-walk Monday smoke would close it.

findings.title: FiscalChainValidator.verifyAuditChainTail walks only TAIL window (default 500). Tamper older than window is invisible to Z.open() integrity assertion
file_line: app/Services/Fiscal/FiscalChainValidator.php:86 $window = Config::get('fiscal.audit_chain_tail_window', 500)
app/Services/Fiscal/FiscalChainValidator.php:118-183 verifyAuditChainTail walks DESC LIMIT then ASC — bounded scan
findings.what_red_disputes: Bounded scan is correct under the 4s z_report_b{N} lock (full O(N) walk would deadlock). BUT the on-demand fiscal:verify-chain command also delegates to the bounded path. A 10M-row tamper at row 5M is invisible to BOTH the daily cron AND the on-demand operator command. Hardening: add `fiscal:verify-chain --full` flag bypassing the window for a quarterly URSSAF-prep full walk, with structured progress output.

findings.title: Best-effort try{Log::channel('fiscal')->...}catch{} swallow leaves no chained trace
file_line: app/Services/Fiscal/ZReportService.php:281-284 swallowed Log::channel('stack')->info('[FISCAL_TIMING]')
app/Services/Order/RefundWithCounterEntryService.php:286-297 + 318-328 swallowed best-effort Log
Note: the audit_logs HMAC chain IS the immutable record; the fiscal Log channel is NOT chained/signed (file/Slack/syslog target depending on config)
findings.what_red_disputes: Swallow is defensible (a log adapter outage must not break a Z close). HOWEVER the comment 'logger swallow leaves no trace' is technically inaccurate because the audit_logs row IS the real evidence and IS written before the log call. The Log channel is observability, not evidence. Sentence-fix: confirmed not a NF525 hole, but a P2 hygiene improvement would route the swallow to a small ring-buffer counter exposed via /api/admin/fiscal/health for ops dashboards.

key_red_disputes: N2 NEEDS_HARDENING (not OK_BY_DESIGN as prior agent framed): no NF525-conformant signed Z PDF blade exists in code, only the JSON bundle. The only printable artefact (EOD synthesis) self-disclaims non-fiscale.
N1 P1 (not silent OK): mitigation is Ansible-side, no in-app boot guard. Out-of-code dependency is a NF525 supply-chain weakness for V1 LOCAL Le Cayenne (owner is sole sysadmin).

ship_block_rationale: V1 LOCAL Le Cayenne can soft-ship today (NF525 chain CHAIN OK empirically, refund + Z mirror + audit chain extension work as designed). N2 PDF gap is a HARD block for any URSSAF day-1 audit but owner-perso V1 LOCAL has weeks/months of soak before any inspection risk crystallises. Recommend creating issues for N2 (this week) and N1 boot guard (V1.0.1) before any V2 / SaaS B2B branch opens.
